Assumption: Models are memoryless; no tunnel states used.
Rationale / Notes: Each individual’s transition depends only on their current state (Markov assumption). Transition probabilities are updated annually by age and risk exposure, implicitly accounting for time-varying hazards.

Assumption: Models stratified by single-year age groups (20–95+), sex (female/male), and calendar year (2019–2050).
Rationale / Notes: Age- and sex-specific risk and mortality rates vary significantly across causes. Temporal stratification allows modeling secular trends and intervention scale-up.

Assumption: Cause-specific Markov models with parallel runs; deaths from other causes modeled after cause-specific.
Rationale / Notes: For each cause (IHD, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, hypertensive heart disease), we simulate transitions including cause-specific mortality and 'other-cause death' as competing absorbing states. Final cause-of-death aggregation is mutually exclusive.
Assumes conditional independence among risk–disease pathways.

Domain: (v) Rationale for Multiplicative Combination of Effects
Assumption: Combined intervention effects are calculated multiplicatively across risk pathways.
Rationale / Notes: Consistent with standard epidemiologic formulation of IR/CF ratios under multiplicative risk assumptions. Avoids overestimating combined effect size vs. additive assumptions; conservative in presence of overlapping risk reductions.
